newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rupee ends down in kerb on dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rupee ends down in kerb on dollar demand.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.04 rupees down at 41.25 against the dollar on Wednesday as demand for the U.S. currency rose after Tuesday's downward adjustment of rupee by the central bank, dealer said.
"The dollar demand remained high today after yesterday's devaluation of the rupee," dealer Owais Kalia said. "People fear the rupee to shed more value in the coming weeks," another dealer said.
The State Bank (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on May 6, was 40.3300/40.5317 to the dollar from 40.2400/40.4412 fixed on April 23.
The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates closed lower at 2.35 percent from 2.40 percent at Tuesday's close.
